reasons: Both correctly explain that -Xmx caps only the heap and that the container's cgroup OOM kill produces exit code 137. B recommends -XX:MaxRAMPercentage, checks that its own memory budget fits 512Mi, and suggests measuring through cgroup memory.current and actuator metrics. A keeps a 512Mi limit with flags whose caps add up to more than 512 MiB (384 heap + 128 metaspace + 64 direct + 128 code cache), and both answers wrongly imply that a heap dump on OutOfMemoryError would capture a container OOM kill.

A: Lists JIT code under Metaspace; compiled code lives in the separate code cache.
Recommended caps (Xmx384m + MaxMetaspaceSize=128m + MaxDirectMemorySize=64m + ReservedCodeCacheSize=128m) exceed the 512Mi limit it says to keep.
Suggests -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError captures state 'before kill', but a cgroup SIGKILL does not trigger it.
B: Section titled 'explicit Xmx' actually uses MaxRAMPercentage instead of -Xmx.
Says a heapdump.hprof can be opened in JFR; JFR/JMC does not open hprof heap dumps (MAT does).
Implies a heap dump will be written on the next container OOM kill, which a SIGKILL does not produce.
